text:
The neighbor would most likely recover for negligence. Leaving gasoline and oil residue on the shop floor, where a repair spark could ignite it, was a failure of reasonable care, and the smoke from that fire discolored the neighbor’s home. Trespass requires intent to cause the entry itself, so an accidental drift of smoke does not qualify, a one-time fire is not a nuisance, and ordinary auto-shop work is not strict liability.

CONFIDENCE: 86
